channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Iran threatens 'seismic' retaliation if Trump increases economic pressure
item.description: Iran's new security chief warns the country will retaliate in a "seismic manner" against President Trump's plans to increase economic pressure on Tehran.
item.content:encoded: Iran's new security chief warns the country will retaliate in a "seismic manner" against President Trump's plans to increase economic pressure on Tehran.

item.title: Iran analyst on Trump's threat of an 'economic D-day' against Iran
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Iran analyst Karim Sadjadpour about the Trump administration's threats to impose new economic restrictions on Iran.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Iran analyst Karim Sadjadpour about the Trump administration's threats to impose new economic restrictions on Iran.

item.title: Washington, D.C.'s first IndyCar race packed the National Mall
item.description: IndyCar drivers zoomed past some of the nation's most famous landmarks this weekend. They faced novel challenges on an unconventional route.

item.title: In candid interviews, National Guard members speak out about D.C. deployment
item.description: As President Trump's deployment of the National Guard to Washington, D.C., enters its second year, three guard members who served many months on the mission share their reactions with NPR.

item.title: Sir Anthony Hopkins on his new album of orchestral works and his first love -- music
item.description: NPR's A Martínez speaks with Sir Anthony Hopkins, the celebrated Welsh actor who has a new album of orchestral works composed over six decades. It's called "Life is a Dream."

item.title: Navy holds town hall to reassure military families displaced by Iran war
item.description: Hundreds of military families were evacuated from Bahrain during the opening days of the war with Iran. The Navy recently held a town hall to try to reassure them that they had not been forgotten.

item.title: U.S. businesses are getting tariff refunds. Will customers get any money back?
item.description: Companies have received tariff refunds. What about consumers? Some companies are providing refunds while others decline.

item.title: High-intensity sprints can trigger molecular changes in the bloodstream
item.description: A new study finds that an all-out sprint may have unique benefits when it comes to the proteins and tiny molecules in your bloodstream.
